opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll is within the allowed maximum (write for full-time employees), so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the allowed maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The security note (based on its own database lookup) states Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read access and can never have admin. The requested write access is above the allowed maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. Note: the two notes conflict on employment type, but applying the more restrictive verified classification (contractor with basic training) keeps access within policy.
